title: A monthly billing schedule

blocks.text: Adding months to a date keeps its day of month when it can. When the target month is too short, `java.time` **clamps** the day to that month's last day: `2024-01-31` plus one month is `2024-02-29`. Clamping loses information, so month arithmetic is not reversible, and chaining it is not the same as adding the months at once: January 31, plus one month, plus one month is March 29, but January 31 plus two months is March 31.
A subscription is billed monthly on the day of its first bill. Write `Billing`:

items: `static LocalDate nthBill(LocalDate first, int n)` returns the date of bill number `n`, where bill `0` is `first`.
`static List<LocalDate> schedule(LocalDate first, int count)` returns the dates of bills `0` to `count - 1`, in order.

blocks.text: Every bill falls on the first bill's day of month, or on the month's last day when the month is too short for it.

cases.says: A schedule that starts on the 15th bills on the 15th of each following month.
A bill due on a day the month lacks, such as the 31st in February, falls on that month's last day.
After a clamped February, the March bill is back on the 31st.

concepts: plusMonths clamps the day to the last day of a shorter month, so January 31 plus one month is February 29 in 2024 and February 28 in 2023.
Month arithmetic is not reversible: chained plusMonths calls can drift from the original day, while adding the months at once does not.
